substack_body_markdown:
CC REPORT / EVENT UNCONFIRMED. Source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, 15 October 2026; week ending 9 October. Commercial crude inventories fell 8.6 million barrels to 415.6 million, while imports fell 791,000 barrels per day. Gasoline stocks rose 3.5 million barrels; distillate stocks fell 2.5 million. These are original EIA balance data retained on 18 October, not a release-time surprise estimate. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

CC REPORT / EVENT UNCONFIRMED. Capital Chronicle analysis: the crude and distillate draws support a qualified supply-buffer watch. Lower imports, a gasoline build and softer four-week gasoline demand oppose a simple broad-demand-boom interpretation. Persistence needs further releases; current market pricing is unobserved. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

CC REPORT / EVENT UNCONFIRMED. Qualified physical-tightness watch over 5 sessions; no current directional entry. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

CC REPORT / EVENT UNCONFIRMED. Over 21 sessions, require several consistent balances before extending the weekly thesis. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

CC REPORT / EVENT UNCONFIRMED. Over 252 sessions, no directional conclusion follows from this weekly draw; evaluate seasonal supply and demand scenarios. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

CC REPORT / EVENT UNCONFIRMED. Retain a research WATCH while subsequent original EIA balances can test persistence; refresh after the next scheduled edition. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

CC REPORT / EVENT UNCONFIRMED. Withdraw the physical-tightness watch if repeated inventory rebuilding accompanies weak product supplied. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]
